case_studies.title: Watch, Remember, Reason: Human-View Video Understanding with MLLMs
case_studies.abstract: Video understanding is being rapidly transformed by multimodal large language models (MLLMs), as research moves from short clips to long, multimodal, and knowledge-intensive video scenarios. These scenarios require models to handle sparse evidence, long-range dependencies, multimodal alignment, and reliable inference under limited computational budgets. This work presents a human-view perspective on LLM-based video understanding, organized around three functional abilities: watching, remembering, and reasoning. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of video understanding using multimodal large language models, building a framework that allows models to watch, remember, and reason about long videos, resulting in improved performance. The framework enables models to handle complex video scenarios with sparse evidence and limited computational budgets. This research is primarily focused on artificial intelligence and machine learning, and is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Pomona: Continuous Code Quality Improvement via Small, Automated Changes at Bloomberg
case_studies.abstract: In this short experience paper, we present Pomona, a lightweight agentic tool that utilises agent skills for continuous automated code quality improvement. Inspired by the philosophy of Kaizen(TM), Pomona automates a cycle of discovery and incremental repair: a Scanning skill identifies improvement tasks (e.g., linting violations, technical debt markers, and test gaps) and prioritises them in a structured backlog, while a Repair skill generates tiny pull requests (PRs) targeting ~10 lines of diff. This human-in-the-loop design enables frequent, low-risk improvements while maintaining engineer
case_studies.summary: Pomona is a tool that solves the problem of continuous code quality improvement by automating small, incremental changes to code, it was built using agent skills and a human-in-the-loop design, and the result is frequent, low-risk improvements to code quality. The tool identifies improvement tasks such as linting violations and test gaps, and generates tiny pull requests to fix them. This improves the overall quality and maintainability of the codebase.

This flags a risk: if your org has large amounts of technical debt or poor code quality, check your codebase immediately for areas where Pomona could be applied.

case_studies.title: The Three-Ring Architecture: Governing Agents in the Era of On-Platform Organisations
case_studies.abstract: The current phase of enterprise AI deployment faces a structural failure: organisations are acquiring agentic capability without the infrastructure to govern it. The result is expected to reproduce the error of the first wave of AI deployment: decentralised intelligence without a federation layer leading to a 95% project failure rate. This paper formalises the Three-Ring Architecture as the governing infrastructure of the on-platform organisation. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of governing artificial intelligence in organisations by introducing the Three-Ring Architecture, which provides a framework for managing AI capabilities. The researchers built a model that consists of three layers: existing production architecture, a federation layer, and a layer based on large language models. The result is a potential solution to reduce the high project failure rate of AI deployments.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI or machine learning projects, here is what to do: review your current architecture, assess the need for a federation layer, and consider implementing the Three-Ring Architecture to improve governance and reduce project failure risk. This flags a risk: if your organisation is deploying AI without a governing infrastructure, check your project failure rate immediately. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but relevant to AI and machine learning projects.
case_studies.score_reasoning: High novelty due to proposed Three-Ring Architecture, high IT relevance as it addresses agentic capability and governance in enterprise AI deployment, but low value for direct real-world implementation within 90 days.

case_studies.title: OpenSkill: Open-World Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
case_studies.abstract: Self-evolving agents requires adaptation after deployment, but existing approaches assume a usable learning loop, such as curated skills, successful trajectories, or verifier signals. Real open-world deployments may provide none of these, offering only a task prompt. In this work, we study open-world self-evolution, where an agent must build both its skills and its own verification signals from scratch, using open-world resources but no target-task supervision. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of self-evolving agents needing adaptation after deployment without curated skills or successful trajectories. The researchers built OpenSkill, a framework that allows an agent to build its skills and verification signals from scratch using open-world resources. The result is a framework that can bootstrap the learning loop without target-task supervision.

case_studies.title: How reliable are LLMs when it comes to playing dice?
case_studies.abstract: We investigate the probabilistic reasoning capabilities of large language models through a controlled benchmarking study on discrete probability problems. We constructed two datasets, respectively a set of standard exercises and a set of counterintuitive exercises, designed to trigger heuristic reasoning, and evaluated 8 state-of-the-art models, each tested with and without Chain-of-Thought prompting. case_studies.summary: This research investigates the reliability of large language models in solving probability problems, finding they perform well on standard exercises but poorly on counterintuitive ones. The researchers built two datasets to test the models' probabilistic reasoning capabilities. The result shows a significant drop in performance on counterintuitive problems, with an average accuracy of 0.59.

case_studies.title: On the Shoulders of Giants: Empowering Automated Smart Contract Auditing via the GiAnt Corpus
case_studies.abstract: High-quality smart contract auditing datasets are crucial for evaluating security tools and advancing smart contract security research. Two major limitations of existing datasets are the manual-induced scalability bottleneck and the deficiency in data granularity and diversity. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited smart contract auditing datasets by building an automated framework called GiANT, which extracts vulnerability insights from real-world auditing reports. The result is a more comprehensive and diverse dataset for evaluating security tools and advancing smart contract security research. This dataset can help improve the security of smart contracts on cloud infrastructure.

A key difficulty lies in credit assignment: agents often receive delayed rewards only at the end of episodes.
